On a cozy little farm, Hattie the barn owl watched the golden evening sun sink behind the hayfields.
Her friend Biscuit the calf came trotting over, his tiny bell making a gentle ting-ting.
Would you like to ride through the sleepy fields, asked Biscuit, pointing to a wagon filled with soft hay.
Farmer's little blue tractor began to roll, carrying the two friends into the lavender evening.
The wagon rocked gently, and the dry hay whispered swish, swish beneath their feet.
Along the fence, sleepy sunflowers bowed their heavy heads toward the earth.
Even the flowers are getting ready for bed, whispered Hattie, but she still folded her little wings.
A family of fireflies blinked softly above the grass, like tiny lanterns saying goodnight.
Biscuit counted little stars one by one, then forgot the numbers with a great big yawn.
Hattie gave a quiet hoo-hoo, and Biscuit answered with the softest little moo.
Their little sounds drifted across the quiet farm, mixing with the rustle of the evening breeze.
Soon the red barn appeared ahead, its windows glowing like two warm golden stars.
The tractor stopped beside the barn, and Biscuit curled into a soft nest of hay.
Hattie tucked her wings around herself and whispered goodnight to Biscuit and the little farm.
And beneath the twinkling stars, the little owl and the sleepy calf dreamed together of another gentle ride.
